title: The Exorcism at the House of Monkton Falls - a spooky and charming co-op game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CufCJMTTKHk

Daniel (@dungeondive) finally films The Exorcism at the House of Monkton Falls, a small Kickstarter he has owned for a few years and describes in one word: charming. A colourless fog has settled over Monkton, Vermont, and paranormal investigators — an FLGS manager, a journalist, a medium, Teddy the dog — must exorcise the manor on the hill by gathering 30 exorcism tokens before dawn.

The mansion is dealt fresh each game: fixed unlocked rooms plus five random locked ones — perhaps a crypt, a yawning portal, a void. Rooms yield abstract tools — grimoires, weapons, occult symbols, keys, candles — assembled into sets to complete tasks like "research demonology" or "steal the blueprints". A wraith starts in the attic, later joined by the Devourer and a bull demon, all steered by darkness cards that also seed rooms with darkness; four tokens shroud a room in fog, and running out of shroud cards loses.

His favourite idea is the lookout system: three spare investigators wait outside, listening to the noises within, and when a character is knocked out one must go in. Solo, you run a primary and a secondary with five shared actions — his carpenter Josh Pitcher started in the garage, the dog Perot in the kitchen. It is essentially Horrified's set collection with the theme pasted on, and Horrified is the better-written game, but the stark black-white-and-red art and the standees fill him with joy. Around $30 on eBay is right.

----

Monkton Falls keeps spare investigators waiting outside the door, listening. Which game handles replacement characters mid-game most thematically?
